title: Things to Do in Tirupati: Tirumala Darshan, Hill Walks & Nearby Temples
seoTitle: Things to Do in Tirupati: Tirumala & Temples | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Tirupati: darshan at the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, climbing the Alipiri or Srivari Mettu footpaths, the laddu prasadam, Akasa Ganga and Papavinasanam, the Silathoranam arch, the Padmavathi Temple, Kapila Theertham, Srikalahasti, Chandragiri Fort and Talakona Falls.
dek: The gateway to Tirumala, one of the world's most visited pilgrimage sites, set in the Seshachalam hills with sacred waterfalls and ancient temples around it.
searchIntent: Pilgrims and families planning a Tirumala darshan trip of one to three days and wanting to know what else to see.
intro: Tirupati, in Andhra Pradesh, lies at the foot of the Seshachalam hills. On the hilltop at Tirumala stands the Sri Venkateswara Temple, dedicated to a form of Vishnu, which receives tens of thousands of pilgrims every day and is one of the richest and most visited religious sites in the world. The temple is run by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD).

The things to do in Tirupati centre on the darshan at Tirumala, often combined with walking up the hill on one of the ancient footpaths, offering hair (tonsure) and collecting the famous laddu prasadam. Around Tirumala are sacred waterfalls and a natural rock arch; in and near the town are the Padmavathi Temple, Kapila Theertham, the Vayu Lingam at Srikalahasti and the fort at Chandragiri.
One to two days is typical. Darshan tickets and accommodation should be booked in advance through the official TTD system.
quickAnswer: Have darshan at the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple
Walk up the Alipiri or Srivari Mettu footpath
Offer hair at the Kalyana Katta
Visit the Padmavathi Temple at Tiruchanur

items.name: Have darshan at Sri Venkateswara Temple

image.alt: Gopuram of the Venkateswara Temple, Tirumala
image.caption: Venkateswara Temple

body: The temple's golden vimana (Ananda Nilayam) rises above the sanctum, and the darshan itself lasts only a few seconds after hours of queuing. Options include free darshan, special entry darshan booked online, and various sevas. Waiting times range from a couple of hours to more than a day at peak times.
A strict dress code applies: traditional clothes such as dhotis or kurta-pyjamas for men and saris or churidars for women. Phones and cameras must be deposited.

facts.Time needed: Half a day to a full day
facts.Good to know: Book darshan and rooms on the official TTD portal

items.name: Walk up the footpath
body: Many pilgrims climb to Tirumala on foot. The Alipiri footpath, about 9 km with thousands of steps, takes around four to six hours; the Srivari Mettu route is shorter and steeper. Both are covered and have water points. Walkers can receive a divya darshan token, subject to current rules.

items.name: Offer hair and collect the laddu
body: Offering hair (tonsure) at the Kalyana Katta is a common vow. The Tirupati laddu, a sweet with a GI tag, is given as prasadam and can be bought in extra quantities at counters.

items.name: See Akasa Ganga and Papavinasanam
body: Akasa Ganga, a waterfall about 3 km from the temple, is said to provide water for the deity's rituals. Papavinasanam, a little further, is a sacred waterfall and dam where pilgrims bathe to wash away sins.

items.name: Visit the Silathoranam
body: The Silathoranam, a natural rock arch near the temple, is a rare geological formation believed to be very ancient. It is set in a small garden.

items.name: See the Sri Vari Museum
body: The TTD's museum at Tirumala has exhibits on the temple's history, rituals and art, including models and old artefacts.

items.name: Visit the Padmavathi Temple
body: The Padmavathi Temple at Tiruchanur, about 5 km from Tirupati, is dedicated to Venkateswara's consort. Tradition says a pilgrimage to Tirumala is complete only after visiting her.

items.name: Bathe at Kapila Theertham
body: Kapila Theertham, at the foot of the hills, is a Shiva temple with a waterfall and a holy pond, especially lovely after the monsoon.

items.name: See the Govindaraja Swamy Temple
body: The Govindaraja Swamy Temple, in the centre of Tirupati, has a tall gopuram and is one of the town's oldest temples.

items.name: Visit Srikalahasti
body: Srikalahasti, about 36 km away, has an important Shiva temple with the Vayu (wind) lingam, one of the five elemental lingams. It is also the centre of Kalamkari, hand-painted textile art; workshops can be visited.

items.name: See Chandragiri Fort
body: Chandragiri Fort, about 15 km away, was a later capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. Its Raja Mahal palace houses a museum, and a sound and light show is held in the evening.

items.name: See Talakona Falls
body: Talakona, about 50 km away in the Sri Venkateswara National Park, is one of the highest waterfalls in Andhra Pradesh, with a forest walk to the falls.

items.name: Brahmotsavam (September or October)
body: The nine-day Brahmotsavam festival brings grand processions of the deity on different vahanams (vehicles) and enormous crowds.

items.name: Vaikuntha Ekadasi (December or January)
body: A special entrance, the Vaikuntha Dwaram, is opened, and devotees throng the temple.

items.name: Summer holidays
body: April to June is very crowded with school holidays and hot. Weekdays outside holidays are calmer.

byTraveller.text: Walk up via Alipiri, have darshan, visit Padmavathi and Srikalahasti.
Book special entry darshan online, stay a night at Tirumala, and visit Akasa Ganga and the museum.
Chandragiri Fort and Srikalahasti's Kalamkari workshops.

oneDay: Take an early darshan slot at Tirumala, collect the laddu, and visit Akasa Ganga, Papavinasanam and the Silathoranam. Come down to Tirupati for the Padmavathi Temple and Kapila Theertham in the evening.
tips: Tirupati has an airport at Renigunta and a railway station; Chennai is about three hours away.
Book darshan and TTD accommodation well in advance on the official website.
Follow the dress code and deposit phones before darshan.
Beware of touts offering quick darshan; use official channels only.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Tirupati?
faqs.a: Have darshan at Tirumala, walk up the footpath, visit Akasa Ganga, Papavinasanam and the Silathoranam, the Padmavathi Temple and Kapila Theertham, and visit Srikalahasti and Chandragiri Fort.

faqs.q: How do I book Tirumala darshan?
faqs.a: Through the official Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams website or app, well in advance.

faqs.q: How long does it take to walk to Tirumala?
faqs.a: The Alipiri footpath takes about four to six hours; Srivari Mettu is shorter.

faqs.q: What is the dress code for Tirumala?
faqs.a: Traditional dress: dhoti or kurta-pyjama for men, and sari or churidar with dupatta for women.
